title_original: A View From the Easel: Vinny Olimpio
excerpt_original: “I use a lot of pigment, and it brings soul and earth to the work.”

blocks.text: Welcome to the 365th installment of A View From the Easel, a series in which artists reflect on their workspace. This week, Vinny Olimpio marks time through his window and plays with the possibilities of pigment.
Want to take part? Check out our submission guidelines and share a bit about your studio with us through this form ! All mediums and workspaces are welcome, including your home studio.
How long have you been working in this space?
A year and a half, since I moved to Lisbon to prepare for my solo show.
Describe an average day in your studio.

I'm an early riser and I arrive with the sun. I always work with it, and I'm blessed to have it blasting through the windows first thing. I usually start with a couple of hours of writing and reworking my symbology, recapping the work from the night before. When I start a new piece, I like to devote myself to it fully for a couple of days, moving back and forth between the writing and the work. I also go out to the garden for moments of contemplation and writing.
